hero.title: A sound app you don't have to browse
hero.intro: I designed, built and launched SoundLax on my own. It is an ambient sound app for focus, rest and sleep, and it runs on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Mac.

links.text: See it on the App Store

image.alt: The SoundLax home screen on an iPhone, held in one hand against a dark background with soft red and blue light

facts.v: Product design, brand, SwiftUI build, launch

p: Before designing anything, I asked twelve friends a simple question: what do you listen to while you work?

items: A white noise playlist on Spotify

blocks.text: Four of the twelve used background sound while they worked, but none of them used a sound app to do it.

p: The need was there, but the apps built for it were not pleasant to open, and people accepted ads and autoplay just to have some rain playing in the background.

So the brief I set myself was [[one place to start a sound within a couple of seconds]], without being sold a programme along the way. Because I was building it on my own, every feature also had to be something I could realistically design, build and maintain myself.

blocks.title: No library on the home screen
p: Most sound apps open on a grid of hundreds of tracks and a search bar. SoundLax opens on four birds instead, each representing a mood: tūī for sharp focus, ruru for deep work, fantail for light and easy, and kererū for relaxing.
People choose how they would like to feel, and the sound is already chosen for them. The full sound list is still one tap away in the bottom bar, with a search to find a particular sound quickly.

image.alt: The Start here section of the SoundLax home screen: four bird cards for Sharp Focus, Deep Work, Light & Easy and Sleep

blocks.title: No player that disappears
p: In the apps I tried, the playback controls disappeared as soon as I moved to another screen.
In SoundLax, the now-playing bar stays at the bottom of every screen, so changing the mix or stopping a sound is always one tap away from anywhere in the app.

image.alt: The now-playing bar above the bottom tab bar, with Home, Sounds, Playlists, Focus and Sleep

blocks.title: No mixer on every screen
p: Some people like to layer rain over café noise and adjust each volume, but most people simply want a sound playing.
For that reason, the mixer sits behind a single card, 'Mix your own set', rather than appearing on every screen. It is there for the people who want it and stays out of the way for everyone else.

image.alt: The Now Playing mixer with Brown Noise, Café Ambience and Soft piano music layered, each with its own volume slider

sections.heading: Inspired by New Zealand's native birds

p: Calm apps often share a similar look, with soft gradients and cool blue and purple palettes. I wanted SoundLax to feel calm in its own way, with a clear connection to where it was made.

Birdsong is part of everyday life in New Zealand, from suburban gardens to native bush, so native birds felt like a natural place to start. I paired vintage naturalist illustrations with [[bold colour, subtle grain and a clean, modern interface]].
Because each bird also represents a mood, the illustrations work as navigation as well as decoration.

bleed.alt: SoundLax visual language: type, colour gradients, sound scenes, bird portraits and a vintage toucan illustration

blocks.title: Focus and sleep
blocks.alt: Four SoundLax screens: a focus timer, a focus task list, adding a task, and sleep settings
blocks.caption: The focus timer pairs a sound with a Pomodoro session. On the sleep screen, a timer fades the sound out, and the alarm fades in gradually rather than going off all at once.

items.text: When I was working or doing housework, I used to search YouTube for background music and often lose 30 minutes doing it. That doesn't happen with this app.
It actually wakes me up like a civilized human being, unlike the default Apple alarm which sounds like a localized nuclear siren designed to trigger a fight-or-flight response.
The sound quality is lovely, especially the rain and nature tracks, and the overall experience feels polished and easy to use.
I just really wish it could auto-save any tweaks I made to existing mixes so they will be ready next time without me having to manually readjust.

p: Not all of the feedback was positive. People asked for more sounds and better balance between them, and several people noticed that Brown Noise cut out briefly each time it looped, first on the Mac version.

One request changed how I thought about customising. I had given people full control to build their own playlists from scratch, but most of them only wanted to start from a playlist that already existed and adjust it. So the app now [[saves those adjustments to the default playlists]], and the next time someone opens a playlist it sounds the way they left it.

The project also made me responsible for a whole product for the first time, from the early research with friends and the design, to building it in SwiftUI with AI assistance, getting through App Store review, setting up subscriptions, and fixing bugs that people found before I did.

blocks.heading: What comes next
p: Because SoundLax is my own product, this case study is not the end of it. I will keep improving the app based on what people tell me and on how they actually use it.
